items.headline: "Impossible To Deliver": Alaska Airlines 787 Long-Haul Flights Are Understaffed, Crews Say
items.facts: The Association of Flight Attendants-CWA filed a grievance claiming Alaska Airlines added new food, drink and premium products to economy cabins without increasing crew staffing levels.

framing.narrativeTitle: Alaska Airlines vs Flight Attendants CWA
framing.publicBrief: The Association of Flight Attendants‑CWA has filed a grievance stating that Alaska Airlines added new food, drink and premium items to economy cabins but did not raise crew staffing levels. The union says the extra service duties overload the current crews, while the airline argues the changes improve the passenger experience without requiring more staff.

roleFlavor.proposer: Alaska Airlines is responsible for cabin service standards and crew scheduling.
roleFlavor.responder: The Association of Flight Attendants‑CWA represents the flight attendants who will have to perform the added duties.

howItWorks: Alaska Airlines can keep the new service items and maintain current crew numbers or agree to add staff.
The union can accept the changes as is or demand additional crew hires.
Both parties see the same contract terms but each controls only their own concession.
If both accept the same proposal, service continues unchanged; if one refuses, negotiations stall.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Select your position on the staffing dispute

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Both sides accept the current arrangement; service continues but crews remain overstretched.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: One side forces a change, leading to either added staff or removal of new items.
outcomes.MIXED: A compromise is reached, adjusting some services or staffing partially.

items.headline: Can Tweaking Plane Routes Cut Aviation’s Climate Impact? An Airspace-Wide Contrail Trial Will Test I
items.facts: A UK-backed trial will test adjusting flight routes over the Atlantic to avoid contrail formation.

framing.narrativeTitle: NATS and Airlines Test New Atlantic Routes
framing.publicBrief: A UK‑backed trial led by NATS is adjusting transatlantic flight paths to stay below the altitude where ice crystals form, aiming to cut the contrail‑induced warming effect. The participating airlines must follow the new corridors or keep their usual routes, and the results will determine whether the approach becomes permanent across European airspace.

roleFlavor.guesser: You are an airline operator deciding whether to adopt the experimental routes or stick to the proven ones.

items.headline: Threatened Bird Species Given Tiny Foot Casts to Help Recovery After Hit by Car
items.facts: Leicestershire Wildlife Hospital staff designed cardboard casts for a whitethroat hit by a car, with the goal of rehabilitating it for release back into the wild.

framing.publicBrief: At dawn, Leicestershire Wildlife Hospital treats a whitethroat struck by a car. Amy Blower and the staff face a choice: use standard splints or design tiny, custom cardboard casts to aid recovery. The goal is to rehabilitate the bird for release back into the wild, but the fragile injury requires precise, gentle support to ensure it survives its confinement and returns to nature.

roleFlavor.contributor: You are part of the Leicestershire Wildlife Hospital team. You hold the materials and the expertise to craft the recovery plan, risking the bird's fragile state on your chosen method of care.

items.headline: Boston Aims to Tackle 100-year Flood Risks with $10 Billion in Infrastructure Projects
items.facts: Boston and the US Army Corps of Engineers released a feasibility study outlining 20 infrastructure projects to protect the city’s coastline from future flood risks.

framing.narrativeTitle: Boston and the Corps Plot New Flood Barriers
framing.publicBrief: Boston and the US Army Corps of Engineers unveil a feasibility study that lists twenty projects aimed at shielding the city’s coastline from century‑scale flood threats. The plan calls for billions in upgrades to seawalls, drainage tunnels and storm‑water pumps. Both parties present the work as essential to protect neighborhoods, commerce and public safety, while the cost and construction timeline draw scrutiny from residents and officials.

roleFlavor.guesser: You coordinate the city’s resilience strategy, reviewing the Corps’ technical proposals and weighing how each project will affect Boston’s neighborhoods and budget.

items.headline: Cursor capitalizes on GitHub frustration, launches rival hosting platform
items.facts: Cursor, now part of SpaceX, launched Origin to rival GitHub for code hosting, targeting developers frustrated by GitHub's outages.

framing.publicBrief: At dawn, the server racks hum with cold light. Cursor, now part of SpaceX, has launched Origin, a rival hosting platform for code. The move targets developers frustrated by GitHub's recent outages. The industry watches to see if the codebase migrates. GitHub holds the established network; Cursor offers a fresh alternative. Developers hold the keys to their repositories, deciding whether to stay put or fork their workflow to the new service. The stability of the ecosystem hangs on this collective shift.

roleFlavor.guesser: You are a developer deciding where to host your code. You see the outages on GitHub and the promise of Origin. Your choice affects your productivity and the broader migration trend.
